title: Interfacial Spin-to-Charge Conversion in Sputtered MoTe2 Heterostructures Probed by Spin Pumping and Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance
authors: J. L. Costa, E. Santos, E. L. T. França, J. B. S. Mendes, A. Azevedo
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and their Weyl semimetal phases, such as MoTe$_2$, have attracted significant attention for spin-orbit torque applications due to their efficient charge-to-spin conversion. However, whether this conversion originates predominantly from the bulk or the interface remains unclear. Here, we investigate spin-charge interconversion in MoTe$_2$ using spin-pumping and spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance (SP-FMR and ST-FMR). Thickness-dependent measurements reveal large spin-to-charge conversion and spin-torque efficiencies that are essentially independent of MoTe$_2$ thickness, indicating that the conversion is predominantly governed by the Rashba-Edelstein effect at the Py/MoTe$_2$ interface rather than by bulk spin transport. This behavior contrasts with the characteristic thickness dependence observed in Pt heterostructures and is further supported by bidirectional SP-FMR and interface-separation measurements. Our results highlight the dominant role of the Py/MoTe$_2$ interface in enabling efficient spin-charge conversion and spin-orbit torques in TMD-based spintronic devices. These findings highlight the potential of sputtered MoTe$_2$/Py heterostructures for low-power spintronic applications, including magnetic memory and logic devices.
summary: This work investigates spin-to-charge conversion in $	ext{MoTe}_2$ heterostructures using SP-FMR and ST-FMR. By analyzing the thickness dependence of the measured signals, the authors conclude that the conversion is dominated by the interfacial Rashba-Edelstein effect rather than bulk spin transport. This highlights the potential of these TMD/ferromagnet interfaces for next-generation low-power spintronic devices.
main_problem: The study aims to determine whether the efficient spin-to-charge conversion observed in $	ext{MoTe}_2$ heterostructures originates predominantly from the bulk material or the interface.
main_result: The spin-to-charge conversion efficiency is found to be largely independent of the $	ext{MoTe}_2$ thickness, strongly indicating that the conversion mechanism is governed by the Rashba-Edelstein effect at the $	ext{Py}/	ext{MoTe}_2$ interface.
method: The research employs advanced spintronic measurements, specifically Spin Pumping Ferromagnetic Resonance (SP-FMR) and Spin-Torque Ferromagnetic Resonance (ST-FMR).
model_or_system: The physical system involves $	ext{MoTe}_2$ (a TMD) bilayers grown on a substrate and coupled with a Permalloy (Py) ferromagnet. The analysis utilizes theoretical models for spin-charge conversion, distinguishing between bulk (ISHE) and interface (ISREE) contributions.
key_observables: Spin-to-charge conversion efficiency ($I_C$), and the dependence of this efficiency on $	ext{MoTe}_2$ thickness ($t$) and applied magnetic field angle ($\phi$).
important_parameters: The thickness dependence of the conversion signal is a key diagnostic tool, contrasting the thickness-independent behavior in $	ext{MoTe}_2$ versus the thickness-dependent behavior in $	ext{Pt}$ reference samples.
main_assumptions: The measured current is assumed to be dominated by the interfacial Rashba-Edelstein effect, and the analysis separates contributions from different physical mechanisms (e.g., bulk vs. interface).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the SP-FMR signals measured as a function of the in-plane applied magnetic field for various $	ext{MoTe}_2$ thicknesses, showing Lorentzian fits and extracted amplitudes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures SP-FMR and ST-FMR signals across varying $	ext{MoTe}_2$ thicknesses, comparing the results against known bulk-dominated systems ($	ext{Pt}$) to isolate the interfacial contribution.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics, the use of advanced resonance techniques (FMR) to probe interfacial electronic properties and spin-orbit coupling mechanisms is relevant to understanding boundary conditions in quantum transport models.

The solid lines correspond to the best fits to the data using Eq. (2). The fits yield IS = -216.8 nA (𝜙= 0°), IS = 213.9 nA (𝜙= 180°), confirming the spin-pumping origin, while IA =- 46.1 nA and IA =10.7 nA, respectively. At 𝜙= 90° , the symmetric signal vanishes as expected. All measurements were performed at an applied RF power of 110 mW.

Figure 2. SP-FMR spectra measured for the reference SiO2/Py(7) film (a) and SiO2/MoTe2(𝑡𝑀𝑜𝑇𝑒2)/Py(7) bilayers with 𝑡𝑀𝑜𝑇𝑒2= 3 (b), 3 (c), 5 (d), 8 (e), 10 (f), 15 (g) and 20 nm (h). The blue and pink symbols correspond to measurements with 𝜙= 0° and 𝜙= 180°, respectively. The solid black curves are fits to Eq. 2. The measurements were carried out at an rf frequency of 9.4 GHz and an rf power of 110 mW.
